To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the mom gene of phage Mu controls an unusual modification of the Mu DNA; 2. the mom gene is expressed only during the early phase of phage development, i.e. after prophage induction but before DNA replication; 3. expression of the mom gene requires an active DNA adenine methyltransferase in the host cell; and 4. the host DNA methyltransferase exerts a novel positive regulatory function in the transcription of the mom mRNA.
the host (E. coli) DNA methylase is required for the expression of a phage Mu gene that controls the mom DNA modification.
the host (Escherichia coli) DNA adenine methyltransferase activity is required in the expression of the mom gene of bacteriophage Mu.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular genetics and biochemistry of the phage mu mom function.
the molecular genetics of DNA modification in bacteria, with special emphasis on the role of DNA methylases in the regulation of gene expression.
the molecular genetics of a DNA modification that controls Mu development in Escherichia coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dam+ DNA adenine methyltransferase is an essential factor for transcription of the Mu mom gene.
the mom gene is transcribed in dam+ cells but not in dam- cells, and that this difference in transcriptional activity is the cause of the difference in the mom function.

the host (Dam+) DNA adenine (6-aminohypoxanthine) methyltransferase activity is essential for transcription of the phages Mu mom gene, and this activity is not required for transcription of other genes in the same Mu genome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mom gene is transcribed only after prophage induction, and that this transcription requires an active host DNA methylase.

Mu development in Escherichia coli is controlled at three levels: (i) the host (dam-) DNA adenine methyltransferase is essential for Mu development; (ii) a host protein (dam+) is required to allow the mom gene to be expressed; and (iii), a host protein (mom+) is required to permit the mom gene to act on the phage DNA
transcription of the mom function in the Mu phage genome requires the host DNA methylase, and that this enzyme acts as a positive regulator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a DNA methyltransferase can act as a transcriptional activator.
DNA methylation is not just an epigenetic modification of DNA.
